description: Every DCGM fault counter for the GB300 estate. Split out of the GPU Health board to keep both boards under 25 panels. Every headline number has an exactly-matching offender table beneath it.

options.content:
GPU Error Surface — ECC, remapped rows, PCIe, limit violations and XID
Every fault counter DCGM publishes for the GB300 estate, each headline number backed by a table that names the exact GPUs, trays, racks and XID codes behind it. Coverage, temperature, power and clocks live on the Coverage board.
GPU area › Area home  ·  Coverage · thermal · power · clocks  ·  Error surface — ECC · XID · violations  ·  NVLink & bandwidth  ·  Readiness checks

panels.title: ECC, remapped rows and PCIe replay

panels.description: A GPU counts once here if any of the eight DCGM error counters below is greater than zero. The offender table beneath names exactly these GPUs — its row count equals this number.

targets.expr: count(count by(node, rack, su, gpu) (label_replace(max by(node, rack, su, gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_ECC_DBE_VOL_TOTAL{cluster=~"$cluster", datahall=~"$datahall", su=~"$su", rack=~"$rack", node=~"$node", gpu=~"$gpu"}) > 0, "fault", "dbe_volatile", "", "") or label_replace(max by(node, rack, su, gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_ECC_SBE_VOL_TOTAL{cluster=~"$cluster", datahall=~"$datahall", su=~"$su", rack=~"$rack", node=~"$node", gpu=~"$gpu"}) > 0, "fault", "sbe_volatile", "", "") or label_replace(max by(node, rack, su, gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_ECC_DBE_AGG_TOTAL{cluster=~"$cluster", datahall=~"$datahall", su=~"$su", rack=~"$rack", node=~"$node", gpu=~"$gpu"}) > 0, "fault", "dbe_aggregate", "", "") or label_replace(max by(node, rack, su, gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_ECC_SBE_AGG_TOTAL{cluster=~"$cluster", datahall=~"$datahall", su=~"$su", rack=~"$rack", node=~"$node", gpu=~"$gpu"}) > 0, "fault", "sbe_aggregate", "", "") or label_replace(max by(node, rack, su, gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_CORRECTABLE_REMAPPED_ROWS{cluster=~"$cluster", datahall=~"$datahall", su=~"$su", rack=~"$rack", node=~"$node", gpu=~"$gpu"}) > 0, "fault", "correctable_remap", "", "") or label_replace(max by(node, rack, su, gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_UNCORRECTABLE_REMAPPED_ROWS{cluster=~"$cluster", datahall=~"$datahall", su=~"$su", rack=~"$rack", node=~"$node", gpu=~"$gpu"}) > 0, "fault", "uncorrectable_remap", "", "") or label_replace(max by(node, rack, su, gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_ROW_REMAP_FAILURE{cluster=~"$cluster", datahall=~"$datahall", su=~"$su", rack=~"$rack", node=~"$node", gpu=~"$gpu"}) > 0, "fault", "remap_failure", "", "") or label_replace(max by(node, rack, su, gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_PCIE_REPLAY_COUNTER{cluster=~"$cluster", datahall=~"$datahall", su=~"$su", rack=~"$rack", node=~"$node", gpu=~"$gpu"}) > 0, "fault", "pcie_replay", "", ""))) or vector(0)

panels.title: GPU fault offenders — the exact GPUs behind the counters above

panels.description: DCGM violation counters are lifetime nanoseconds spent throttled below the requested clock. A GPU counts once here if either counter is greater than zero. The table below names exactly these GPUs. Units: these DCGM counters accrue in NANOSECONDS on this fleet, not the microseconds the DCGM docs list. Proven empirically: on example50-dh01-h04-37 gpu 1 the low-utilisation counter advanced 3,593,599,858,112 over 3,600 s of wall clock = 0.998 units per nanosecond of elapsed time. A microsecond reading would imply 998 seconds of throttle per second, which is impossible.

targets.expr: count(count by(node, rack, su, gpu) (label_replace(max by(node, rack, su, gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_THERMAL_VIOLATION{cluster=~"$cluster", datahall=~"$datahall", su=~"$su", rack=~"$rack", node=~"$node", gpu=~"$gpu"}) > 0, "viol", "thermal", "", "") or label_replace(max by(node, rack, su, gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_BOARD_LIMIT_VIOLATION{cluster=~"$cluster", datahall=~"$datahall", su=~"$su", rack=~"$rack", node=~"$node", gpu=~"$gpu"}) > 0, "viol", "board_limit", "", ""))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Limit-violation offenders — the exact GPUs

panels.description: Rate of change of the two cumulative violation counters, summed over every GPU in scope. The unit is nanoseconds of throttle accrued per wall-clock second, so 1 s here would mean one GPU throttled continuously. Flat at zero means nothing is being throttled right now. The GPUs behind any non-zero reading are the ones listed in "Limit-violation offenders" to the left. Power-cap and reliability accrual are owned by the Readiness checks board, which carries their own backing table. Counter units verified empirically as nanoseconds, not the microseconds the DCGM docs list.

targets.expr: sum(rate(DCGM_FI_DEV_THERMAL_VIOLATION{cluster=~"$cluster", datahall=~"$datahall", su=~"$su", rack=~"$rack", node=~"$node", gpu=~"$gpu"}[10m]))
sum(rate(DCGM_FI_DEV_BOARD_LIMIT_VIOLATION{cluster=~"$cluster", datahall=~"$datahall", su=~"$su", rack=~"$rack", node=~"$node", gpu=~"$gpu"}[10m]))
